senses.gloss: geya, nt. (= Pali geyya), the second in the traditional Pali-BHS list of nine (in Mvy twelve) types of Buddhist [] sacred literature, classified by form and content; mingled prose and verse: (sūtraṃ) geyaṃ (Mvy gey(y)aṃ, but Mironov only geyaṃ) (vyākaraṇaṃ …) Mvy 〔1268〕; Dharmas 〔62〕; (sūtrāṇi … gāthā itivṛttakaṃ jātakam adbhutaṃ ca,) nidāna … geyaṃ ca bhāṣāmi tathopadeśān SP 〔45.(7—)8〕 (vss). Tib. on Mvy dbyaṅs kyis bsñad pa, app. narration with verses.

Geya-rājan, n. or title of a cakravartin: Mvy 〔3593〕; first element confirmed by Tib. glu dbyaṅs, song. The adjoining parallel names, all ending in -rājan, suggest that Geya- was a locality; perh. cf. Geyamālava or -marthaka (?), Kirfel, Kosm. 〔74〕 (from Purāṇas).
